figures.finding: A director employed on an Australian screen production is covered by the Broadcasting, Recorded Entertainment and Cinemas Award 2020, which sets a binding weekly minimum: A$1,548.80 (A$40.76 an hour) for a Level 9 director of series, serials, documentaries or animation, and A$1,619.30 (A$42.61) for a Level 10 director of features, mini-series and telemovies, from 1 July 2026.

value.instrument: Broadcasting, Recorded Entertainment and Cinemas Award 2020 [MA000091]

level9.work: series or serials, documentaries, animated productions

level10.work: feature film, mini-series and one shot drama/telemovie

figures.applies: Australia, directors engaged as employees in the industry (the award covers employers and their employees in its classifications); a director engaged as an independent contractor is outside it.

sources.said: 4.1 This industry award covers employers throughout Australia in the broadcasting, recorded entertainment and cinema industry and their employees in the classifications set out in this award to the exclusion of any other modern award. … 13.3 Adult rates [13.3 varied by PR729350 , PR740777 ; PR749974 ; PR749974 ppc 30Jan23, PR762200 , PR773980 , PR786630 , PR799371 ppc 01Jul26] … An employer must pay adult entertainment employees in the classifications in clause 13.2 the following minimum rates for ordinary hours worked by the employee (subject to the provisions of clause 13.8 ): Classification level Minimum weekly rate (full-time employee) Minimum hourly rate … Grade 17 1548.80 40.76 Grade 18 1619.30 42.61 … (q) Grade 17 entertainment employee includes the following classifications: Motion Picture Production Employee Level 9. (r) Grade 18 entertainment employee includes the following classifications: Motion Picture Production Employee Level 10. … G.1.9 Level 9 A level 9 employee will demonstrate advanced industry skills as a Director working in series or serials, documentaries, animated productions or similar productions. … G.1.10 Level 10 A level 10 employee will demonstrate advanced industry skills as a Director working in feature film, mini-series and one shot drama/telemovie productions.

figures.finding: The Australian Directors' Guild's series rates are recommended minimum standards, not an agreement: the guild publishes them for scripted series directors.
figures.applies: Australia, scripted episodic broadcast, online and streaming series; not serials or one-off telemovies.

sources.said: This document sets out recommended minimum standards of pay and conditions for Screen Directors in Australia.

figures.finding: The ADG recommends a series director's minimum weekly fee by episode budget: A$4,000 (under A$900K per half-hour or A$1.8M per hour episode), A$6,000 (to A$1.5M / A$2.5M), A$8,000 above, and dollar-for-dollar DGA parity on international productions, about 3% of budget.

bands.rule: AUD 1 per USD 1 of DGA rate

figures.applies: Australia, ADG recommendation 2025-26 for scripted series; plus superannuation at or above the guarantee.

sources.said: Band 1: Low Budget Under $900 K Under $1.8 M $4,000 Band 2: Mid Budget $900 - $1.5 M $1.8 M to $2.5 M $6,000 Band 3: High Budget over $1.5 M Over $2.5 M $8,000 … approximately 3% of a production’s budget, bringing episodic directors’ fees into parity with the rates and conditions accorded to screenwriters

figures.finding: The ADG recommends pre-production no shorter than the shoot (an 8-week shoot gets 8 weeks of prep), two more weeks for a set-up or pilot director, overtime past 12 hours a shoot day, and an unimpeded Director's Cut of 3 days per half-hour and 5 days per hour episode.
figures.applies: Australia, ADG recommendation 2025-26 for scripted series.

sources.said: i.e. A director on an 8 week shoot will have a minimum of 8 weeks of formal pre-production. A setup or pilot director is entitled to an additional 2 weeks of pre-production, … A director is entitled to a minimum of 3 days unimpeded editing time per half-hour episode, and 5 days per one-hour episode, to prepare a ‘Director’s Cut’.

figures.finding: ADG full membership costs A$550 a year (established: two directing credits and two hours of credited screen time) or A$275 (emerging: one publicly screened short and 20 minutes), for Australian citizens or permanent residents.

figures.finding: English is the working language; in the 2021 Census about 5.66 million people used a language other than English at home.

sources.said: The number of people who used a language other than English at home has increased by nearly 800,000 (792,062) from 2016 to over 5.5 million people (5,663,709).
